No Japan Ministry of Foreign Affairs visa-fee page could be fetched. Every MOFA URL attempted returned HTTP 403 to this client (mofa.go.jp/mofaj/toko/visa/short/study.html, mofa.go.jp/mofaj/toko/visa/fee.html, mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/procedure/fee.html, mofa.go.jp/j_info/visit/visa/procedure/pagewe_000001_00391.html, mofa.go.jp/mofaj/toko/visa/tetsuzuki/pagew_000001_02672.html), as did overseas mission mirrors (emb-japan.go.jp, id/th/vn.emb-japan.go.jp, uk.emb-japan.go.jp). Search-result snippets suggested MOFA consular fee figures exist and were revised with effect from 1 July 2026, but a snippet is not a fetched page, so no value is recorded. Japan also uses a Certificate of Eligibility route administered by the Immigration Services Agency, whose fee schedule is separate from MOFA consular fees and was not fetched either.

Japan does not publish a national minimum cash threshold for a student visa or Certificate of Eligibility. The government-approved Study in Japan site (JASSO) states only that proof of ability to pay may be requested and lists the document types, with no monetary figure: 'When applying for a COE or visa, you may be asked for proof that you are able to cover your expenses while studying in Japan. Required documents: Financial sponsor's (the person wishing to study in Japan or their guarantor) savings balance certificate, income certificate covering the past year, documentation identifying sources of funds, etc.' The only money figures found in official material are living-cost averages, not visa thresholds: 'Total expenditure: 105,000 yen' per month national average, source '2023 Lifestyle Survey of Privately-Financed International Students (JASSO)' (https://www.studyinjapan.go.jp/en/life/cost-of-living, fetched). Per-university screening amounts (for example Nagoya University G30's JPY 1,000,000, or Waseda CJL's JPY 1,920,000 per year) appear only in university documents, which are institution-set and not a national rule, so they are not recorded as a country-level figure.

colliding_values.statement: MEXT publishes, in the statutory salary-level disclosure of a Japanese national university corporation, the model salary for age 22 as '月額 220,000円 年間給与3,634,400円' - that is, a starting salary for a university graduate of JPY 220,000 per month. This is a GROSS monthly figure. It is the '大卒初任給' (new-graduate starting salary) for the public national university sector.

MEXT publishes, in the same model-salary table, '○30歳（助教：博士修了初任給） / 月額 370,370円 年間給与6,212,766円' for a teaching assistant post at the age-30 doctoral-completion starting salary. Recorded only to show the scale spread in the same official table; note this is age 30, not an entry-level graduate salary.

sources.notes: The page is served by the Immigration Services Agency of Japan. The English-locale request returned the Japanese original of the 'Student' status of residence permission page; the verbatim Japanese above is the operative text. The official name of the permission is 資格外活動許可 / Permission to Engage in Activities Outside Those Permitted Under the Status of Residence Previously Granted, split into a blanket permit (包括許可, 28 hours or fewer per week) and an individual permit (個別許可). Holiday relaxation is 8 hours per day during the educational institution's long vacation. The agency page carries no effective date, so as_of is recorded as the retrieval year 2026. I did not fetch a MOFA source on the post-graduation job-seeking route, so no claim is made about that.

sources.notes: The University of Tokyo is a national university and the page is its own official fee table. Confirmed: undergraduate annual tuition is JPY 642,960 for the current cohort (the JPY 535,800 line on this table applies to undergraduates who enrolled in or before 2024, and to graduate students from other categories), plus a one-off admission fee of JPY 282,000. The same university page lists a separate, current national-university-wide comparison elsewhere, but I only report what appears in this fetched table. No course-level differentiation exists on this page (it is faculty-wide). I did not verify a private-university figure from an official page.
